reason: The hypothesis directly mirrors the findings of the single cited paper (E1, E2). E1 confirms the baseline coercivity, the 40-fold increase with RTA alone, and the 3 orders of magnitude increase with Pt addition and L10 ordering. E2 supports the emergence of magnetic anisotropy and the role of the L10 phase. All key premises are accurately represented by the cited evidence.
premises: As-deposited FeCoNiMnCu HEA thin films are magnetically soft with coercivity ~10 Oe
RTA alone on FeCoNiMnCu films increases coercivity ~40-fold
Adding ~50 at.% Pt and RTA forms an ordered L10 phase
The L10 phase formation leads to high magnetic anisotropy and 3 orders of magnitude coercivity increase
The mechanism is enhanced magnetocrystalline anisotropy from the ordered L10 phase impeding domain wall motion
